items.main: LEFT JOIN produces (1, NULL) and (NULL, NULL). WHERE B.Y IS NULL keeps both. However, ordinary equality in ON: 1=NULL is NULL (no match), NULL=NULL is NULL (no match). Both left rows are unmatched, so both have B.Y NULL.
items.main_reason: Both left rows have no true ON match. The join rows are (1,NULL) and (NULL,NULL), and the right-side IS NULL test keeps both. Its explicit comparison results are correctly stated as NULL.

choice_feedback.explanation: Incorrect: The NULL row in A also has B.Y NULL after left join and passes the filter.

choice_feedback.explanation: Incorrect: The row with A.X=1 is unmatched (1=NULL is false in ON), so B.Y is NULL and it passes.

issues.reason: SQLite evaluates 1=NULL to NULL. ON accepts only true, so NULL gives no match without becoming false. The main explicitly and correctly says this comparison is NULL.
issues.interpretation_note: False in ON could be intended as operational shorthand for no match; the actual nonmatch is correct. As learner-facing literal explanation of NULL handling, it conflates false with unknown and is not fully supported.

choice_feedback.explanation: Correct: Both A rows are unmatched in the join (no ON equality holds), so both have B.Y NULL and satisfy WHERE.
choice_feedback.reason: Neither left row has a true equality match, and both NULL-extended B.Y values pass WHERE.

choice_feedback.explanation: Incorrect: LEFT JOIN guarantees all A rows appear; with no matches, B.Y is NULL for both.
choice_feedback.reason: The LEFT JOIN stage preserves each unmatched A row with NULL on the right; in this query the stated IS NULL filter also preserves them. The guarantee is read as about the join stage.
